reasons: Claimed status is compliant with no redline or comment, which is the expected output shape; the cited §4(a) supports that classification.

Customer convenience right exists: either Party may terminate 'for any reason' following the one-year Initial Term on 90 days' notice — within the fallback's 60–90 day window, so the failed 'Customer convenience termination present' regex is a phrasing variant, not a substantive gap.

Term is a 1-year Initial Term with 1-year auto-renewals, so the 'no Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months' trigger is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in; the mid-Initial-Term bar is symmetric and equally restrains the Vendor.

No early-termination fee or penalty on the Customer: Kubient is only entitled to fees generated during the 90-day notice period while still performing, and under the §5 revenue-share model payments flow from Kubient to AP, so the absent pro-rata prepaid-fee refund is inapplicable.

Vendor's convenience right is on exactly 90 days' notice, i.e., not 'fewer than 90 days', so it stays out of walk-away territory; that it runs any time after the Initial Term rather than only at term end is correctly noted as a sub-element short of the fallback/preferred wording rather than escalated, consistent with the playbook's classification semantics.
